evidence_type: AI decision support (Nemotron) on reported cases; not an operational instruction

context.product: FlyWithEase: Track C detects where GPS is failing from aircraft integrity reports; Track A6 confirms which nearby airport can absorb diversions (Noida International Airport, Jewar, ~70 km from Delhi IGI, phase 1 inaugurated 28 Mar 2026, one runway); Track B3 proposes a LEO navigation layer (19 dB stronger, simulated spoofed error 50 m -> 8 m); passenger recovery flow rebooks, books care at the right city and tracks bags.
context.airline_finding_reported: ICAO-hosted airline presentation: some receivers need a ground maintenance reset after interference; IATA: receiver recovery can exceed 30 minutes in a significant number of cases.

cases.title: Delhi IGI: GPS spoofing on Runway 10 approaches (2025)
cases.facts: Flights on GPS-based (RNP) approaches to Runway 10 were spoofed. Contingency procedures were used; conventional aids (ILS) remained available for other runway directions; government reported no effect on movements; DGCA introduced real-time spoofing reporting.

nemotron.fails: GPS spoofing on RNP approaches to Runway 10 at Delhi IGI causes lateral deviation, forcing diversion to alternate airport.
nemotron.turnaround: Late inbound from diversion; receiver reset/maintenance check adds 30+ minutes ground time before next rotation.
nemotron.passengers: Delayed departure; rebooking to alternate airport; baggage misrouting risk from disrupted ground ops.

options.con: Not available for Runway 10; increases runway occupancy time
options.decision: Use conventional ILS for Runway 10 if available; otherwise divert to Noida International Airport (Jewar) with FlyWithEase Track A6 monitoring.

nemotron.decision: Divert to Noida International Airport (Jewar) using Track A6 confirmed capability; runway 10 ILS unavailable, RNP spoofed, Jewar has one runway ready for diversion.
fix: Activate FlyWithEase Track C GPS integrity warnings for crew awareness
Use Track A6 to confirm Jewar airport diversion availability and runway status
Deploy passenger recovery flow to rebook affected passengers to correct city and track bags

human_review.note: Facts say ILS stayed available on other runway directions and movements were unaffected. First move: switch arrivals to an ILS runway at IGI; divert to Jewar only if that runway is saturated.
human_review.final: Move arrivals to an ILS runway at IGI; Jewar is the fallback, confirmed by Track A6.

cases.title: Amritsar / Jammu: persistent jamming near the border
cases.facts: 276 reported incidents in north-western India in 2025; Track C shows a band of high-interference cells along the India-Pakistan border. Aircraft lose GPS en route and on approach; some arrive with receivers that do not recover before the next departure.

nemotron.fails: GPS jamming in north-western India causes aircraft to lose GPS en route and on approach to Amritsar/Jammu, compromising safe landing and missed approach capability.
nemotron.turnaround: Inbound aircraft delayed by receiver reset/maintenance checks after jamming; crew duty limits may be exceeded before next rotation can begin.
nemotron.passengers: Passengers experience flight diversions, delays, or cancellations; baggage may be mishandled during rebooking to alternative airports.

options.pro: Avoids jamming zone; uses proven runway
options.con: Increases fuel burn and crew duty time

options.pro: May allow landing at origin airport
options.con: Risk of missed approach if receivers do not recover; safety critical

options.pro: New runway designed for CAT III operations; outside jamming zone
options.con: Longer ground transit for passengers; slot availability uncertainty

nemotron.decision: Diversion to Noida International Airport using Track A6 confirmed capability; avoids persistent jamming and leverages new runway capacity.
fix: Activate Track C jamming warning for all aircraft in sector
File diversion plan to Noida International Airport with ATC
Use B3 LEO backup receiver during final approach phase
nemotron.confidence: medium Three-step fix relies on untested LEO backup performance

human_review.note: Diverting away from the jamming band is sound. "CAT III" at Jewar is not in our data, so check Jewar's approach aids before dispatch. B3 is a future system, not available today.
human_review.final: Divert away from the jamming band (Jewar or Delhi), after checking approach aids; use Track C to warn every flight in the sector.

cases.title: Complete GPS outage at an airport with GPS-only approaches
cases.facts: 10% of reported Indian incidents were complete outages and 6% lost GNSS-based landing capability. Scenario: an evening bank of arrivals into an airport whose only instrument approach is GPS-based, poor visibility, nearest alternates Delhi IGI and Jewar.

nemotron.fails: GPS-only approach fails in poor visibility, preventing landing and forcing diversion to alternate airports.
nemotron.turnaround: Late inbound arrival delays turnaround; receiver reset and maintenance check add 30+ minutes ground time before next rotation.
nemotron.passengers: Passengers experience diversions, delays, missed connections, and overnight stays at alternate airports.

options.pro: Nearest viable alternate with runway capacity
options.con: Requires runway availability and ATC clearance not guaranteed
Fuel exhaustion risk, crew duty limit breach

options.action: Proceed to Delhi IGI with manual backup
options.pro: Larger airport with multiple approach types
options.con: 70 km distance, possible slot loss, ATC workload

nemotron.decision: Diversion to Jewar airport as nearest alternate with runway capacity for GPS-based approach.
fix: Activate FlyWithEase Track C GPS integrity warnings for crew awareness
Coordinate with ATC for Jewar runway availability and approach clearance
Use passenger recovery flow to rebook affected passengers to next available flights

human_review.note: Diversion is right. Jewar must have a non-GPS approach (ILS) for this to work; check before naming it as the alternate.
human_review.final: Divert to the nearest alternate with a non-GPS approach (Delhi IGI ILS, or Jewar if confirmed); start passenger rebooking before landing.

cases.title: Tartu, Estonia: route suspended (Apr-May 2024)
cases.facts: Finnair suspended Helsinki-Tartu flights from 29 April to 31 May 2024 because GPS interference made the GPS-based approach unusable; Tallinn Airport was unaffected. Passengers had to reroute via Tallinn by road.

nemotron.fails: GPS interference disables the GPS-based approach at Tartu Airport, making the approach unusable for aircraft relying on satellite navigation.
nemotron.turnaround: Late inbound aircraft cannot execute the approach; receiver reset and maintenance checks add delay before the next rotation can begin.
nemotron.passengers: Passengers face rerouting via Tallinn by road, causing delays and additional ground transport costs.

options.action: Use B3 LEO backup for approach guidance

nemotron.decision: Choose diversion to Tallinn Airport because it is unaffected by the interference and ensures safe approach without receiver reset delays.
fix: Activate FlyWithEase Track C warnings to monitor interference extent
Diversion to Tallinn Airport using established procedures
Implement passenger recovery flow to rebook onto Tallinn-bound flights

human_review.note: Matches what actually happened: flights stopped at Tartu and passengers went via Tallinn. Our addition: start the rebooking and coach transfer before departure, not after.
human_review.final: Operate to Tallinn and pre-book the road transfer and rebookings before departure.

review_note: Each Nemotron decision was checked by the team against the reported facts; corrections are shown next to the AI output.
